messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Elevated 502/504 rate detected in ca-central-1 gateway pool (gateway-ca-*/proxypool). Alerts: 5xx-rate > 8% over 3m. Paging rota: ryan_sre_oncall.

ryan_sre_oncall: acked. I'm on my way — grabbing logs and checking dashboards.

maria_ops: seeing similar spike from monitoring: gateway latency jumps ~300ms -> 1.2s, errors mostly 502 with some 504. TCP resets up slightly. No deploys in ca-central in last 40m according to deploy-bot.

ingrid_engineering: heading into the pool to check upstream health (mlworker pools + kvcache). Preliminary: NLB metrics show increasing 502s to ml-infer-ca-01 node group.

ryan_sre_oncall: running quick probe to a couple gateways and a backend.

> ryan_sre_oncall run: 
> curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' https://gateway-ca.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}' --max-time 5
> *result:* connection reset / 502 html from proxy on 3/5 attempts, 1 timed out.

alex_platform: no config changes in the routing tier. I'm checking capacity on dedicated ca pools: GPU pools show 95% CPU on some infer nodes, memory stable. Autoscaler hasn't triggered because of sticky routing.

maria_ops: customer impact: subset of requests are failing. Error distribution: 72% from ca-central edge, 25% from ca-central dedicated, 3% misc. Affected customers flagged: 4 high-traffic tenants show increased 5xx and increased client retries.

olivia_product: pinging CS to prep comms. John, can you pull a list of affected accounts and any active escalations?

john_csm: on it. I've DM'd the CS leads for the four tenants. No active public incidents yet, but two customers reported higher latency in their dashboards.

ingrid_engineering: quick root hint — looks like kv-prefix cache invalidation storms at ca kvproxy causing occasional high tail latencies on the request path. When kvproxy is slow, backend inference times out and proxy returns 502. Logs show repeated prefix-miss cascades starting ~2812345200.

ryan_sre_oncall: can you show the kvproxy logs?

ingrid_engineering: past 5m snippet: 
```
2024-10-03T12:40:05Z kvproxy[ca-01] WARN prefix_fetch_timeout id=0x7f3a path=/model/abc kv_get timeout=1200ms
2024-10-03T12:40:07Z kvproxy[ca-02] ERR upstream_hang id=0x9a1c fetch_retries=3
2024-10-03T12:40:09Z kvproxy[ca-01] WARN miss_bloom id=0x7f9e heavy_load=true
2024-10-03T12:40:12Z mlworker[ca-04] ERR accept_timeout request_id=0x1ff
```

ryan_sre_oncall: ok that matches the pattern. Hypothesis: a hot-prefix storm causing cache thrashing; slow backend fetches cascade to gateway 502s. Two mitigation paths: 1) patch routing to fallback traffic away from ca-central to us-east read-only mode for non-data-local customers; 2) reduce prefix fetch pressure by enabling local-cache read-through fallback and temporary increased cache TTLs on kvproxy.

alex_platform: we can do both. Immediate short-term: shift non-SLA traffic from gateway-ca to gateway-useast with a traffic steer for 20% -> 70% based on customer tags. I'll open the routing shift and start with 30% to be safe.

ryan_sre_oncall: please do: include health checks and gradual ramp. Post plan in thread.

alex_platform: plan: 
- create route-rewrite rule: if customer.tag != "data-local" && route == /v1/generate, set prefer_region=us-east
- start 30% steer for 2 minutes, monitor 5xx rate, then 70% if stable
- if 5xx persists in us-east, rollback to 0% immediately

deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-rule-2024-10-03-1402 (safe-preview) -> will apply in 15s.

maria_ops: starting dashboard watch. setting alert mute on ca-central to reduce noise for paging while we test steer (muting only noisy alert group).

(30s later)

alex_platform: steer applied at 2812345300 -> 30% traffic to us-east. Monitoring: overall 5xx reduced to 4.1% from 8.7% in ca-central aggregated. Latency on us-east increased slightly but still within SLO.

ryan_sre_oncall: good. Now for KV mitigation — ingrid, can you flip cache-ttl bump on kvproxy in ca to reduce backend fetch frequency? Prefer a conservative change: TTL x3 for hot-prefixes and enable read-through fallback to in-memory if remote fails.

ingrid_engineering: prepared a hotfix patch. Command: 
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/kvproxy-ca && kubectl patch configmap/kvproxy-config -p '{"data":{"hot_ttl_multiplier":"3","enable_local_fallback":"true"}}'
```
I will apply to canary nodes first (kvproxy-ca-01), then roll the rest.

ryan_sre_oncall: go for canary. I'll keep the steer at 30% until we see stable 5xx < 2.5%.

(2m later)

ingrid_engineering: canary applied at 2812345600. Logs: fewer prefix_fetch_timeout events on ca-01. 502 rate in ca-central down to 3.8%.

alex_platform: ramped steer to 70% at 2812345720. Systemwide 5xx now trending 1.9% and counting.

maria_ops: customer impact update: affected tenant metrics improved; no new support tickets in the last 5m. Marking customer impact as degraded but contained.

john_csm: I've sent an initial DM to affected customers describing mitigation and that we're investigating root cause; offering to pull request logs if they see continued issues.

olivia_product: we should consider a post-incident note for customers that had retries beyond 5%. Please tag affected tenants.

ryan_sre_oncall: good call. Next: we need to decide permanent fix: patch kvproxy bloom/miss behavior or add a hot-prefix sharding. Ingrid, propose action items for next 48h.

ingrid_engineering: initial proposals: 
- implement prefix sharding (medium effort, 2-3 days) to avoid hot-key storms;
- improve cache metrics and early cold start smoothing;
- add circuit-breaker on gateway to failover to pre-warmed us-east variants earlier;
- make hot_ttl_multiplier config adjustable via runtime flags for quick tuning.
I'll draft RFC and timeline.

ryan_sre_oncall: handoff time in ~25m. @alex_platform can you take oncall for the remainder? I'll do postmortem capture and timeline.

alex_platform: I can take the handoff. I'll monitor for 60m and keep steer rules in place at 30% for non-data-local customers, ready to scale down.

deploy-bot: routing-rule-2024-10-03-1402 toggled -> active.

ryan_sre_oncall: summary for handoff: 
- Root symptoms: elevated 502/504 in ca-central driven by kvproxy hot-prefix cache thrashing causing backend timeouts.
- Immediate mitigation: traffic steer to us-east (30% -> 70% -> 30% steady), kvproxy TTL multiplier x3 + local fallback, canary rollout confirmed stable.
- Customer impact: degraded for a subset of tenants (4), now improving; no major data loss; CS notified.
- Next actions: ingrid to RFC prefix sharding; alex to hold oncall; ops to coordinate postmortem and customer note.

alex_platform: ack and taking over. If we see reversion to >2.5% 5xx I'll trigger full 100% steer to us-east and coordinate emergency maintenance.

maria_ops: adding post-incident timeline ticket: INC-2024-CA-0007 and assigning to ingrid+ryan for RCA.

(40m later)

alex_platform: monitoring steady. 5xx: ca-central 1.2% (mostly retries), route health green. Holding steer at 30%.

john_csm: customers confirmed improved experience. One tenant asked for a short post-incident summary — I'll coordinate with product for wording.

ryan_sre_oncall: closing pager for now, leaving handoff note in the incident ticket. Will follow up on RFC. Thanks all. :pray:

incident-bot: Incident marked as acknowledged -> mitigated. Incident ticket INC-2024-CA-0007 created by maria_ops.

alex_platform: leaving final comment in the ticket and locking this thread for operational updates; reopen if new regressions occur.

ryan_sre_oncall: final timeline note appended to ticket.
